text:
eli: Heads-up — after pushing the new kernel selector heuristic (rollout 0.46) we see a 9-12% P99 latency regression on Qwen-7B for seq=1024 workloads. Perf CI alerted. Attached profile snippet below.

maria: ugh. Is this the tiled-attn -> fallback path? Any evidence it's picking a suboptimal kernel for RoPE-scaled models?

eli: yep tiled->generic fallback. Profiling top hotspots (sampled):
```
0. kernel_select::score 34%
1. copy_kv_tiles 21%
2. generic_attn_forward 18%
3. kv_cache_lock 7%
```

sanjay: perf-ci shows the attn suite failing: https://ci.redwood/suites/attn/1872 - regressions flagged >5% across batched throughput. Failing traces seem concentrated on Mixtral variants with head_dim 64.

eli: interesting — failing samples are mostly mixtral-8x with head_dim=64 and rope_scale=1.2. Selector cost model currently assumes tiling helps when head_dim >= 96. That threshold looks wrong for these tiling kernels.

maria: quick mitigation: add a selector override to prefer legacy (non-swapped) kernel for (model.family contains "mixtral" && head_dim == 64) and run smoke evals. Also run quality checks — we saw token-level diffs when switching kernels in earlier experiments.

eli: agreed. temp selector patch:
```
selector.override_rules:
  - if model.family == 'mixtral' and head_dim == 64:
      prefer: legacy_tiled
```

perf-ci-bot: [alert] perf/regressions/attn-suite failed on commit a1c3f2. P99 increased by 11% on qwen-7b seq=1024 throughput test.

sanjay: I'll push the override to canary for 2 hours and monitor token-diff evals. If quality drifts, we'll rollback. @maria can you run the eval harness on the failing prompt set (evalset: attn_rope_regression_v2)?

maria: running now — kicked off 4k prompts, beam=1. If we see >0.5% delta in top-1 accuracy vs baseline we'll cut a rollback.

eli: also instrumenting a probe around kv_cache read path to check copy vs view usage; suspect extra memcopy when switching kernels causing lock contention and higher tail latency.

maria: first 500 prompts done — token-diff 0.18% and small perplexity bump. Within noise, but a handful of long-range prompts show more significant decode diffs / hallucination increase.

sanjay: can you paste a minimal repro where decode diverges?

maria: minimal repro snippet:
```
Prompt: "Summarize the data patterns across years 2010-2020 with emphasis on long-term trends..."
Baseline: "...consistent upward trend in sales and engagement."
Curr: "...sharp fluctuations driven by short-term spikes."
```

eli: that pattern suggests numerical differences introduced by kernel accumulation/reduction order interacting with RoPE scaling. The swap changed accumulation order and combined floats differently; quantized paths amplify small differences.

sanjay: proposed plan:
1) Canary override for mixtral head_dim=64 (immediate).
2) Add regression unit test in eval harness for the long-range prompt set (attn_rope_regression_v2).
3) Refit selector cost-model: prefer tiled kernel when head_dim <= 64 AND seq >= 512 (flip threshold).
4) Re-run perf CI and the token-diff suite.

maria: start rollback criteria: token-diff >0.5% absolute or >5 hallucination cases per 4k prompts.

perf-ci-bot: canary deployed to cluster:growth-canary. Monitoring: p99 down ~6% vs regressed commit.

eli: FYI I opened PR with the selector threshold fix + comments about rope_scale sensitivity: https://git.redwood/p/runtime/PR-2345 — includes microbench for head_dim variations and a note to re-evaluate quantized accumulation paths.

sanjay: after 1 hour on canary we look stable on perf and token-diff metrics. Will promote the patch to staging and schedule a follow-up to train a small selector ML model (instead of hand thresholds) with head_dim, seq, rope_scale as features.

maria: leaving a release note: "Guard: kernel-selector now defaults to legacy tiled kernel for Mixtral variants with head_dim=64 to avoid rare decode differences caused by kernel-switch numerical reshuffle."

eli: :thumbsup:
